summary: This work demonstrates direct resonant control of a superconducting cavity using flux-tunable Jaynes–Cummings interactions, achieving preparation of arbitrary Fock state superpositions and Givens rotations between cavity levels. The implementation integrates broadband on-chip flux delivery with cascaded Chebyshev filtering to protect the cavity lifetime at $T_1 = 590 ± 40$ µs while enabling nanosecond-timescale transmon frequency tuning.
motivation: Standard dispersive bosonic cQED requires complex numerical control pulses to address cavity transitions since excitation levels are nearly degenerate within each qubit manifold. Direct access to resonant Jaynes–Cummings transitions would enable analytically simple, faster control of bosonic qudits while preserving cavity coherence.
method: A 3D superconducting cavity ($\omega_\mathrm{cav}/2\pi = 6.868$ GHz) couples to an asymmetric DC-SQUID transmon ($g/2\pi = 12.2 ± 0.1$ MHz, $\gamma = E_{J2}/E_{J1} = 4.02$) with flux bias delivered through an on-chip CPW line featuring two cascaded third-order Chebyshev low-pass filters (cutoff 4 GHz) achieving 98 dB attenuation at cavity frequency. Sequential and multi-tone drives address individual JC ladder transitions, followed by adiabatic detuning of the transmon to map JC eigenstates onto Fock states.
result: Deterministic Fock state superposition preparation ($\frac{1}{2}(|0\rangle + |3\rangle)$ with $93 ± 3\%$ fidelity, $640$ ns) and Givens rotations $\hat{\mathcal{R}}_{n_A,n_B}(\theta)$ between arbitrary Fock pairs ($|1\rangle$ to $|4\rangle$ with $68–80\%$ fidelity depending on $\theta$) were demonstrated, with gate times fundamentally faster than dispersive SNAP/GRAPE by factors of 5–20 due to interaction strength scaling as $g \gg \chi/2\pi \approx 1.62$ MHz.
